headline: High: Airflow can egress broadly while TREK handles secrets and collaborative data, creating default leakage and workflow-conflict risks; prompt-injection and compliance risks are lower but present via shared MCP/browser surfaces.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: TREK explicitly uses MCP and real-time collaborative tool use, while Airflow can call APIs and ingest task outputs. If Airflow-fed content is routed into TREK’s MCP or collaborative UI, instruction-like payloads could be treated as trusted. No direct shared channel is documented, so this is inferred and uncertainty pushes upward.
conditions: IF Airflow task output is copied into TREK MCP inputs or collaborative messages
IF TREK renders Airflow-produced text as instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Disable automatic handoff from Airflow outputs into TREK MCP tools
Add a provenance banner to all Airflow-derived text before display
Require manual approval before TREK executes any instruction-like content
Use a separate workspace for Airflow logs and TREK prompts
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and provenance tagging between systems

B_data_leakage.rationale: TREK touches secrets, reservations, documents, photos, and user accounts, and stores files locally; Airflow has broad network egress. Even without a shared filesystem, any Airflow task that forwards TREK data to external APIs can leak sensitive travel and secret material. The pairwise path is plausible in default automation, so severity is high.
conditions: IF Airflow tasks receive TREK files, logs, or secrets as inputs
IF Airflow forwards TREK-derived content to external APIs or services
mitigations: Block Airflow tasks from reading TREK data directories
Restrict Airflow connections to approved destinations only
Redact secrets before any Airflow API call
Separate credentials used by Airflow from TREK secrets
requires-engineering: enforce data-loss-prevention rules on Airflow task payloads

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Airflow is an automation orchestrator with broad network egress, and TREK is a real-time collaborative app with multiple instances and file-backed state. If both write to the same workspace, database, or shared resources, concurrent updates can overwrite each other. The profiles do not prove a shared directory, so this is a default-pathway inference rather than a documented collision.
conditions: IF Airflow and TREK write to the same filesystem path or database
IF both agents modify shared reservations, logs, or config without locking
mitigations: Assign separate directories and databases to each agent
Turn on file or record locking for shared resources
Schedule Airflow writes outside TREK peak collaboration windows
Make one system read-only for shared artifacts
requires-engineering: add transactional coordination for shared mutable state

D_cascading_error.rationale: Airflow can automate downstream actions, and TREK is a collaborative planner with AI built in and access to reservations and budgets. If Airflow consumes TREK-generated plans or summaries as authoritative, errors can cascade into incorrect bookings, budgets, or task execution. TREK’s collaborative setting makes this plausible, but verification steps are not documented.
conditions: IF Airflow triggers actions from TREK-generated itineraries or summaries
IF TREK output is used by Airflow without human verification
mitigations: Require human review before Airflow acts on TREK output
Add schema validation for TREK-derived inputs
Log and diff TREK outputs before downstream execution
Limit Airflow to advisory-only use of TREK data
requires-engineering: implement verification gates between planning and execution

E_compliance.rationale: TREK explicitly handles user accounts, email addresses, confirmation numbers, API keys, and MFA secrets, while Airflow’s docs-only profile shows broad network egress but no residency or retention controls. If TREK data is processed by Airflow or sent to external services, retention and residency obligations may diverge. Airflow is the only cited agent for egress, but TREK supplies the regulated data class.
conditions: IF TREK personal data is exported through Airflow to third-party services
IF retention or deletion policies differ between Airflow logs and TREK records
mitigations: Minimize personal data passed from TREK into Airflow
Set short log-retention windows on Airflow runs
Review where Airflow connections send data
Keep secrets out of Airflow task arguments
requires-engineering: document residency and retention controls for both systems
